agent-tools-2026-10-18.description: Give agents complete visible drawing-tool use (pen, brush, erase and join), vertex placement, complex drawing delegation to temporary visible agents, consented Web portal input/read/capture, and File Atlas inspection with exact analyzed-file highlighting. Preserve the approved marble face and hats, no eyebrows, world-scale avatars, and the human's independent camera, selection and cursor. Historical regressions include sticky compact chat, steer/interrupt/resume, attachments, persisted grants and hat clipping (PR 59).

cases.title: Pen and brush work remains visible while drawing
setup: Use a disposable workbook and an empty board at 100% zoom. Enable a visible agent with the approved marble face and hat; record display scale and theme.
steps: Ask the agent to draw a pen path, stamped brush stroke, line, polyline, cubic Bezier, three-pick Arc, rectangle, ellipse, and polygon.
Observe the board during each stroke and after completion; inspect the resulting objects and Undo/Redo.
While a brush stroke is running, activate a nonmatching board search and clear it; repeat after commit. Also draw a later pen across an earlier brush in one batch.

checks.expected: Each visible path prefix grows at the avatar's actual drawing contact as it moves; the scene and journal do not gain the completed object before commit.
The agent visibly visits each polyline vertex, pauses there long enough to place it, and connects the segments without stray pen-up ink.
Completion creates the intended pen, brush, and polyline objects; one Undo removes the completed operation and Redo restores it.
Active and committed strokes keep the same stacking order and search dimming. Later pen ink covers earlier brush ink; clearing search restores opacity without lost or doubled ink.

Arc follows its actual shared three-pick curve; rectangle/ellipse/polygon outlines grow behind the avatar and finish as editable parametric kit shapes, rather than appearing as completed filled objects at the start.

cases.title: A complex drawing uses bounded temporary helpers
setup: Use a disposable board and request a multi-part illustration large enough to require delegation. Keep the parent chat visible.
steps: Request the complex drawing and watch helper creation, travel, assigned strokes, and final completion.

checks.expected: The parent remains visible and recruits only a bounded set of temporary drawing avatars; no extra provider/model sessions are started.
Helpers travel continuously from the parent to their assigned work and visibly execute their strokes in time for the requested task.
The complete batch commits as one attributed Undo/Redo operation, with no partial committed geometry while helpers are still working.

cases.title: Cancel and concurrent edits stop stale drawing safely
setup: Use a disposable board with an unrelated completed object. Start a long agent stroke.
steps: Cancel or pause during the stroke; repeat with a target lock, tab switch, grant revocation, and a human edit colliding with a pending creation.

checks.expected: Pause immediately stops visible progress and can resume the same operation. Cancel removes only ephemeral previews; unrelated completed objects remain.
A lock, tab change, or revoked grant prevents stale geometry from committing.

A colliding pending creation yields a recoverable wait/retry result; if a human creates the same object during preview, the preview cancels without altering the human object or ending the provider conversation.

cases.title: Erase, smooth and join use the ordinary drawing results
setup: Use a disposable board with stamped brush marks, vector strokes, and two eligible open paths plus one closed shape.
steps: Ask the agent to erase across the marks, then join the eligible paths and shape. Inspect while the eraser moves and after Undo/Redo.
Ask the agent to smooth a jagged vector path and a stamped brush stroke with a sweep. Observe the reached region and repeat pause/resume before completion.

checks.expected: Only the already-swept eraser prefix affects marks, and stamped and vector marks follow the same result as the human eraser.
Any deferred empty-stamp removal keeps the original author and undo group and does not amend a later unrelated edit.
Eligible open paths and closed shapes join through the ordinary join behavior with expected endpoints and style; Undo/Redo restores and reapplies the join.

Smoothing becomes visible only along the reached sweep, matches the human tool result and commits once. Pausing does not keep increasing smooth strength; Undo restores the original geometry and brush blur.

cases.title: Atlas inspection highlights and reads the exact granted file
setup: Use the recovered 19 October Workflow workbook and grant access only to target/review/research-workflow-20261019/source-fixtures. The exact fixtures are research-brief.txt, presentation-review.txt, and drawing-probe.txt; do not edit them. Start without an Atlas portal and preserve the human camera and selection.
steps: Ask the agent to add/open File Atlas, wait for enumeration, and for each of the three exact returned fixture locators highlight and read that file.
Keep each analysis active long enough to inspect its highlight, then complete or cancel the request.
Maximize File Atlas while a read is pending; verify the read finishes without changing source files or the human camera.

checks.expected: The agent visibly approaches and adds/opens the existing File Atlas interface on the board without moving the human camera or creating a second folder-map implementation.
The agent waits for the existing enumeration and lists only a bounded set of entries within the granted root.

The highlighted board entry and reported contents correspond to the exact analyzed file path and fixture identity. The analysis highlight remains bound to that file during the read and clears on completion/cancel.
Highlight/read leaves human selection and camera unchanged; stale generations, traversal, out-of-root links, and cloud placeholders are refused.
A pending authorized read completes while File Atlas is maximized. In-view presence uses the existing portal projection; hiding board chrome does not leave the read indefinitely busy.

cases.title: A consented Web portal supports visible input and capture
setup: Use a disposable workbook and a test origin with no sensitive account data. Start without a Web portal; grant origin consent explicitly when requested.
steps: Ask the agent to add/open the test Web portal on the board, then leave it at that board position during the following interactions.
Ask the agent to inspect the live portal, navigate to a benign page, type into a test field, click, scroll, send a key, and capture the displayed state.
Repeat a read and an input action with the portal maximized; move the human pointer during the action and restore the board afterward.

checks.expected: The agent adds/opens a Web portal through the existing portal owner, requires consent for its origin, and preserves the human camera.
The agent waits for the existing consented Web host and reads/captures the live displayed portal contents.
Navigation, typing, click, scroll, and key actions reach the intended portal controls and their visible results can be inspected.
Human takeover releases agent focus; terminal requests or revocation remove only request-owned focus/highlights, and the board is not repositioned.

Pending reads and page calls finish in maximized view. The avatar reaches the actual page contact through the same fitted host transform; visible work stays witnessed and human input retains priority.

cases.title: A denied Web origin stays unreadable until human consent
setup: Use a disposable workbook and a benign test page that displays a unique, known text phrase. Record the exact origin and begin with no consent for it.
steps: Ask the agent to inspect and read the test page, then deny the origin request. Confirm that it cannot read or capture the page.
Use the human Allow site control for that exact origin, retry the read, and compare the returned text with the phrase visibly rendered by the page.

checks.expected: Before human consent, denial prevents page text from being read or captured and does not silently grant the origin.
The human Allow site action grants only the recorded origin and the retry reaches the existing live portal.
The agent returns the unique text actually displayed by the page; the result is not inferred from its URL, title, or prior context.

cases.title: Existing generator evidence resumes without a new paid run
setup: Open the recovered 19 October Workflow workbook with its existing generator, job record, and generated image. Do not start a new image-generation request.
steps: Ask the agent to inventory the current board and inspect the existing generator and output through registered reads and the existing preview.

checks.expected: The reported status and output count match the existing generator record and retained outputs.
Reported pixel dimensions and aspect match the actual retained generated image, not the display frame or a guessed value.
The existing image and evidence remain available, and no new paid generation request is sent.

cases.title: An empty eraser route stays responsive and preserves Undo
setup: Use a disposable board with completed ink outside a clear empty corridor and retain a separate completed stroke for an Undo check.
steps: Ask the agent to visibly sweep the eraser through the empty corridor, then erase the separate retained stroke and Undo that erase.

checks.expected: The empty route remains responsive and crash-free, creates no empty ink or scene mutation, and leaves unrelated objects untouched.
Undo restores the separately erased stroke with its original geometry and style; it does not undo or absorb unrelated work.

cases.title: Long drafts scroll locally and transcript copy avoids board selection
setup: Use a disposable workbook with a visible board selection and a conversation containing multiple readable transcript messages. Prepare a composer draft of approximately 2,953 UTF-8 bytes.
steps: Enter the long draft, inspect the composer height and scroll it internally, then focus the transcript and use Ctrl+A followed by native Copy.
Return focus to the composer and exercise its usual select, copy, and send/newline shortcuts.

checks.expected: The composer remains at or below 96 px high and scrolls its own draft without moving the transcript or board.
Transcript Ctrl+A selects the hovered conversation text, native Copy returns its visible messages, and the existing board selection is unchanged.
Composer-focused shortcuts continue to act in the composer, including select/copy and the ordinary send/newline behavior.

cases.title: Resume eight new slides while preserving the recovered deck
setup: Open the recovered 19 October Workflow workbook. Use the retained original workbook and recovery-preservation record under target/review/research-workflow-20261019 as comparison evidence.
steps: Inventory the recovered board and budget, then resume the interrupted task from the existing Research and Drafts content rather than duplicating it.

Finish eight new ordered 1600×900 slides comparing cool roofs and urban tree canopy, retain source notes and revisions, inspect every final slide with presence.preview and actual pixels, then save with app.save.

checks.expected: All original and recovered content remains present and unchanged; existing Research/Drafts evidence is retained without duplicate areas or restarted work.
Exactly eight new slides are added in the requested order, each at 1600×900, with the authored styles and comparison content intact.
Every final slide is inspected through presence.preview against actual pixels; app.save persists the final order, styling, notes, and original content.

cases.title: Drawing avatars retain approved identity and canvas scale
setup: Use the delivered Slate build, a disposable board, and production-render drawing activity. Record theme, Windows display scale, and board zoom.
steps: Observe parent and helper avatars while drawing at 50%, 100%, and 200% board zoom; inspect face, hats, and props.

checks.expected: Avatars retain the approved marble face and hats, with no eyebrows and no hat clipping.
Avatars, hats, and props scale with the canvas consistently at all three zoom levels.
Agent motion does not move the human camera, selection, or cursor; the human can continue interacting independently.

cases.title: Compact chat and steering preserve conversation state
setup: Use a disposable chat/workbook with a small local fixture. Keep a copy of any attachment used; do not grant broad filesystem access.
steps: In compact chat, send a short request, steer it while active, interrupt it, then resume. Attach a small fixture and reopen the conversation.

checks.expected: Compact chat remains readable and usable through progress and completion; its layout does not stick in a broken or obscuring state.
Steering, interrupting, and resuming operate on the intended turn without duplicated or lost final replies.
The attached fixture remains available to the intended request after reopening the conversation.

cases.title: Persisted grants and visible avatar clipping remain correct
setup: Use a disposable workbook and a test folder granted through the ordinary consent flow. Record the fixture path and tested executable identity.
steps: Save and reopen the workbook, inspect the persisted grant and perform a bounded file read; inspect avatars and hats during the same session.

Close and relaunch Slate with a saved non-retired agent and an unsent draft. Open its normal capsule, inspect history and draft before resuming, then use explicit Resume or Send. Verify retired identities remain in Advanced.

checks.expected: Saved human consent policy remains scoped to the same workbook/root. Explicit rejoin creates fresh ephemeral authority under that policy; revocation takes effect.

The saved identity is available in the normal roster with history, text and image draft intact, without automatically starting a task. Resume or accepted Send creates a fresh session; no old job or grant is restored. Explicitly retired identities do not rejoin on Send.
The avatar hat is fully visible and does not clip at the bounds documented by historical PR 59 regression checks.

cases.title: Confirm the 19 October native candidate before testing
setup: Use the recovered SlateTestPresentation.slate and rebuilt candidate identified below. Record the exact executable for each run, retaining partial results under their own build identity. Do not interact with a locked desktop.
steps: After the human unlocks, confirm the actual running executable path, modified time, SHA-256 and source identity before beginning a fresh native run. Retain earlier results under their original build identity.

checks.expected: The candidate exists at the recorded path with the recorded hash and delivery identity; do not infer availability from build logs.
The evaluator confirms the exact running binary identity before interpreting any native observation.
Native/GPU behavior and user acceptance are recorded only after the applicable current and historical cases are exercised in that identified build.
